method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts' (online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481)), 20 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC10152565). S2: QUOTED from Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437) 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method' (published 30 October 2022), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC9656447). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every Wave 7 claim from S1 (European panel 2023) unchanged and adds S2, the Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Delphi statements (2022, CC BY 4.0, quoted), for patient education and dosing schedules, lid-margin disease and the ocular surface around eye surgery. The TFOS management summary (© Alcon/TFOS) was again not used.

claims.claim: **Dry eye disease is common (about 11–30% of Europeans)** and harms vision, quality of life and work, with a physical and psychological toll.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tear hyperosmolarity is taken to be the starting event,** from excess evaporation or low tear production; it damages the surface directly and by setting off inflammation, which keeps the cycle going.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Grade severity on five things** (unanimous panel view): symptom burden, staining of cornea and conjunctiva, reduced tear secretion, a fast tear break-up time, and meibomian gland disease.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Is it dry-eye keratitis at all?** New vessels, anterior-chamber cells and flare, or stromal oedema point to another keratitis or keratopathy (interstitial, neurotrophic, bullous). Ciclosporin trials selected severe dry-eye keratitis on fluorescein staining, symptoms and Schirmer testing.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for systemic disease:** Sjögren's syndrome carries the strongest link, then other immune and rheumatic conditions (rheumatoid arthritis, lupus), small-fibre neuropathy, chronic pain states and chronic graft-versus-host disease.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Escalate step by step** — environmental measures, artificial tears, lid hygiene, then topical steroid and/or topical ciclosporin — whether or not there is systemic disease.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ciclosporin, like topical steroid, is second-line:** for when tear substitutes, lid hygiene and environmental changes have failed.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Base the decision to start ciclosporin on** how much the cornea and conjunctiva stain, immune-related systemic disease, a quick response to steroid, and poor control on standard care. Other risk factors can justify it even without severe corneal staining.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Its licensed use is severe keratitis only;** earlier use is off-label, which the panel found the most contested point (79.3% agreement).
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Topical steroids break the inflammatory cycle quickly but only for short courses,** because of raised IOP, cataract and opportunistic infection. Fluorometholone, loteprednol and hydrocortisone are less likely to raise IOP or cause cataract.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ciclosporin, unlike steroid, is safe to use long term.**
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bridge with a steroid:** start ciclosporin together with the steroid or up to a week after it, and taper the steroid on the signs and symptoms of inflammation. In trials the steroid ran 4–8 weeks before tapering; the fast steroid covers ciclosporin's slow onset and improves how well it is tolerated.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Watch the pressure on steroid:** check IOP after 1–2 weeks. There is no set review interval on combined treatment; base it on the steroid's type and strength, how often it is used, and comorbidities.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review response at 1 month, then every 3 months.** Improvement may start in the first month but is usually seen at 6–8 weeks.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Even with an early response, keep going;** discourage stopping early.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep using artificial tears alongside ciclosporin;** a lubricant 15–20 min before and/or after the dose markedly reduces burning and stinging.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Continue indefinitely while it works and is tolerated;** tapering or stopping is an option after sustained improvement (61% had not relapsed at 24 months in SANSIKA follow-up). Stop for poor tolerance or no effect.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No need to stop ciclosporin for eye surgery:** a healthy ocular surface before cataract or glaucoma surgery improves results.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Warn about stinging at instillation,** the commonest side effect; it is usually mild to moderate and few patients stop because of it. Systemic absorption is negligible.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tell patients the benefit is slow** (possibly several weeks), since people often stop once symptoms first ease or when nothing seems to happen. Storage: do not freeze, keep in the original pack away from light.
claims.locator: Messmer EM, Ahmad S, Benitez del Castillo JM et al. (European DED expert panel), European Journal of Ophthalmology, 'Management of inflammation in dry eye disease: Recommendations from a European panel of experts', online 5 December 2022; issue 2023 (doi 10.1177/11206721221141481), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10152565/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Teach patients that dry eye is chronic and fluctuating, and prescribe a planned dosing schedule that fits their lifestyle** (97.1% agreement) rather than leaving treatment decisions to them.
claims.source_text: the qualitative discussion led to 97.1% acceptance of the first statement: "The most important aspect for recognizing and treating signs and symptoms of dry eye disease is educating patients about its chronic nature. Furthermore, it should be stressed the need for a dynamic treatment by proposing a programmed dose schedule that also takes into account patients' lifestyle." … once patients have been educated about the disease, it is important to establish a planned therapeutic regimen rather than leaving treatment decisions up to the patients themselves.
claims.locator: Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437), 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method', published 30 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9656447/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Avoid 'as needed' dosing and belittling words like 'droplets':** call it a tear substitute or artificial tear, and explain that treatment targets the cause, not the symptom felt at the time.
claims.source_text: Given that patients usually do not understand that DED is a chronic condition and are inclined to underestimate the importance of treatment, it was stressed that diminutive words such as "droplets" should be avoided in favor of more appropriate terms such as "tear substitute" or "artificial tear". The posology regimen "as needed" was also criticized because it suggests that patients can autonomously decide when a symptom should be treated, whereas there is a need for continuous ocular surface nutrition regardless of patient's ocular discomfort []. It was also considered important to explain that treatment is not prescribed to treat the perceived symptom but in order to treat the underlying cause of the symptom.
claims.locator: Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437), 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method', published 30 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9656447/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Fit treatment to the patient's environment, work, diet and the season.**
claims.source_text: It was also pointed out that treatment should be adapted to the environment in which patients live, to the work type and place, to the diet and also to the seasonality.
claims.locator: Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437), 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method', published 30 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9656447/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Prescribe, do not suggest:** give clear instructions on how, when and how often to use each medicine.
claims.source_text: Good treatment adherence requires clinicians to prescribe (and not suggest) medications and give clear instructions about how, when and how frequently to administer them
claims.locator: Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437), 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method', published 30 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9656447/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Dry eye is often linked with anxiety and depression;** consider assessing mood and quality of life, at interview or with self-completed questionnaires, which also helps track the effect of treatment.
claims.source_text: some of the clinicians said it was also important to assess psychological variables, as DED is often associated with depressive syndromes. Such assessments could be made as part of a patient interview but also by using self-completed questionnaires that evaluate patient depression and anxiety scores as well as their quality of life. … This may not only improve patient's subjective perceptions but also allows monitoring the effects of treatment on symptoms and the patients' subjectively perceived quality of life.
claims.locator: Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437), 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method', published 30 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9656447/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Lid-margin problems that do not need surgery can cause or worsen dry eye.** Treat them with lid hygiene, topical corticosteroid, specific topical and/or systemic antibiotics and tear substitutes, tailored to the lid and surface changes, disease stage and patient (100% agreement).
claims.source_text: led to 100% acceptance of the second statement: "Problems of the eyelid margin that are not of surgical interest may cause and/or exacerbate dry eye disease; they should be treated with hygienic treatments, topical corticosteroid medications, specific topical and/or systemic antibiotics, and tear substitutes in a personalized manner, depending on the nature of the change in the eyelid margin and ocular surface, the stage of the disease, and the type of patient."
claims.locator: Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437), 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method', published 30 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9656447/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Start lid hygiene while the meibomian glands are still present;** once they have become atrophic, treatment is unlikely to help.
claims.source_text: pointed out the importance of educating patients about hygienic treatments and the need to use them when the meibomian glands are still present, before the eventual progression towards an atrophic process, when any therapeutic action is likely to be useless.
claims.locator: Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437), 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method', published 30 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9656447/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Ocular surface disease is a risk factor for poorer surgical results and postoperative adverse events:** assess and treat the surface before, during and after eye surgery (100% agreement).
claims.source_text: led to the formulation of the third statement with 100% acceptance: "Ocular surface abnormalities may be a risk factor for poorer surgical outcomes and postoperative adverse events. It is important to evaluate and treat the ocular surface before, during and after surgery in order to optimize surgical outcomes"
claims.locator: Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437), 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method', published 30 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9656447/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tell patients about any dry-eye signs found before surgery,** so later problems are not blamed on the operation, and postpone surgery if needed until the surface disease is well controlled. Surgical technique (such as where corneal incisions go) can be adapted to protect the surface.
claims.source_text: They stressed the importance of informing patients of the presence of any preoperative DED signs so that any eventual postoperative problem is not considered a direct consequence of the surgery. In addition, they agreed on the importance of treating DED before surgery and, if necessary, postponing the operation until the treatment is successful and the ocular surface disease well controlled. … It was also agreed that the ocular surface should also be examined and treated after surgery and that, in some cases, the surgical technique (e.g., the location of corneal incisions) may be modified in order to better protect the ocular surface.
claims.locator: Aragona P, Giannaccare G, Mencucci R, Rubino P, Cantera E, Rolando M et al. (Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group), Journal of Clinical Medicine 11(21):6437 (doi 10.3390/jcm11216437), 'The Management of Dry Eye Disease: Proceedings of Italian Dry Eye Consensus Group Using the Delphi Method', published 30 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9656447/, retrieved 2026-09-24
